title: Clone Graph

content.problemStatement:
You're given a connected, undirected graph with `n` nodes labeled 1 through n, as an adjacency list `graph`, where `graph[i]` is the list of neighbor labels for node i + 1 (so `graph[0]` holds node 1's neighbors, `graph[1]` holds node 2's neighbors, and so on).

**Build a deep copy of the entire graph, meaning every node and every edge is a brand new object, not a reference to the original.**

To prove the clone is structurally correct, re-derive its adjacency list from the cloned graph you built (not from the input) and return it, with each row's neighbors sorted in ascending order and rows ordered by node label.
constraints: the graph is connected (every node is reachable from every other node)
no self-loops and no repeated edges
the adjacency list is symmetric: if node a lists node b as a neighbor, node b lists node a
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: a 4-cycle: node 1 connects to 2 and 4, node 2 connects to 1 and 3, and so on; the clone reproduces the same connections
a single node with no edges clones to a single node with no edges
a triangle among nodes 1, 2, and 3; the input row order within each list doesn't matter, only the resulting sorted adjacency does

hints: Identify the search space and verify that the condition is monotonic (true...true...false...false).
Be mindful of integer overflow when computing mid: use mid = left + (right - left) // 2.
Ensure the termination condition (left <= right vs left < right) correctly handles boundary elements.
learningObjectives: Master core algorithmic concepts and pattern recognition for Clone Graph.
Analyze time and space complexity trade-offs to meet optimal constraint benchmarks.
Formulate robust solutions addressing edge cases including boundary values and empty sets.
